---
title: "Validation Rules"
---

The IR validator enforces structural correctness before any writer runs.

Every error carries a rule id, a location (section, row group, row, column), and a
message. Rule ids are the strings below, both in `Display` output (`[COL_COUNT] …`)
and when errors are serialized.

## Version

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `IR_VERSION` | `ir_version` isn't `MAJOR.MINOR` (ASCII digits, as in `"1.0"`), or its major version isn't 1, the one this gridwell reads. Checked first. A newer minor version (`"1.3"`) is valid, with a [warning](#a-newer-minor-version); see [Versions](index.qmd#versions) |

## Limits

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | `config.table_cols` > 16,384, a section has more than 1,048,576 rows, or the table has more than 50 million cells. Checked after the version; the other checks are skipped when a limit is exceeded. Limits are configurable from Rust (`validate_with_limits`). |

## Structural Rules

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `COL_COUNT` | Every row (header, data and summary) has exactly `config.table_cols` cell objects; spanned positions hold placeholders |
| `ROW_COUNT` | `thead` has `config.header_rows` rows; data rows (not summary rows) total `config.body_rows` |
| `COLSPEC_LENGTH` | `column_spec` has `config.table_cols` entries |
| `STUB_CONTIGUOUS` | The stub is a block at the left: `config.stub_cols` is at most `config.table_cols`, and no cell flagged `is_stub` starts to the right of the stub columns |
| `STYLE_REFS_VALID` | Every `style_id` refers to a style definition or composition, wherever it appears: header lines, columns, rows, cells, group labels, notes and `styled_text` nodes. A composition's `extends` refers to a definition (not a composition) |
| `FOOTNOTE_REFS_VALID` | Every `footnote_mark` refers to a defined footnote, wherever it appears: cells (including summary rows), header lines, group labels, and the notes themselves |
| `SUMMARY_REQUIRES_STUB` | A group with summary rows requires `config.stub_cols >= 1` |
| `UNKNOWN_VALUE` | A keyword field holds a value outside its allowed set (see [Keyword values](#keyword-values)) |
| `INVALID_COLOR` | A color field is not a CSS color (see [Colors](#colors)) |
| `INVALID_LENGTH` | A length field does not parse, or uses a form its field does not allow (see [Lengths](#lengths)) |
| `INVALID_STYLE_ID` | A style id (a key of `styles.defs` or `styles.compositions`) is empty or uses a character other than ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-` |
| `DUPLICATE_ID` | Two footnotes have the same `id`, or a style id is a key of both `styles.defs` and `styles.compositions`: a reference to it would be ambiguous |
| `INVALID_LANG` | `config.lang` is not a well-formed BCP 47 language tag: subtags of ASCII letters and digits separated by `-` (`fr-CA`, not `fr_CA`), as in `ar`, `zh-Hant-TW`, `es-419` or a private-use `x-…` tag |
| `INVALID_HREF` | A text run's `href` is not a link gridwell writes: an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host, or a `mailto` URL with an address, without whitespace or control characters (the scheme matched ignoring case). Other schemes, such as `javascript:`, `data:` and `file:`, could run code or open a local file when the link is followed |
| `INVALID_TABLE_ID` | `config.id` is not an HTML id: it is empty or has whitespace |

## Span Rules

Spans are checked per section: the header, each group's data rows, and each group's
summary rows. A span never crosses a section.

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `SPAN_ZERO_VALUE` | `colspan` or `rowspan` is 0 |
| `SPAN_OVERFLOW_RIGHT` | `col + colspan > table_cols`: span exceeds the right edge |
| `SPAN_OVERFLOW_BOTTOM` | `row + rowspan > section rows`: span exceeds the section |
| `SPAN_OVERLAP` | Two spans claim the same `(row, col)` position |
| `SPAN_PLACEHOLDER_MISMATCH` | A placeholder that no cell's `colspan` or `rowspan` covers |
| `SPAN_GAP` | A grid position with no cell object at all. A row with too few cells is already reported as `COL_COUNT` (and its section's spans are then not checked), so `validate()` reports this only through `OccupancyGrid::materialize` used directly |
| `SPAN_PLACEHOLDER_HAS_CONTENT` | A placeholder cell has non-empty content |

## Keyword values

Keyword fields are matched ignoring case and surrounding whitespace, and the aliases
below are accepted. An unrecognized value still parses: it is kept verbatim (and
round-trips unchanged) and reported as `UNKNOWN_VALUE`, so every bad value is listed
at once. Known values are written back in their canonical spelling.

| Field | Allowed values (aliases) |
|-------|--------------------------|
| `column_spec[].align`, `text_align` | `left` (`start`), `center` (`centre`), `right` (`end`), `justify`, `char` |
| `vertical_align` | `top`, `middle`, `bottom`, `baseline`, `super`, `sub` |
| `row.role` | `column_label`, `spanner_label`, `summary_row` (`summary`), `grand_summary_row` (`grand_summary`) |
| `cell.scope` | `col`, `colgroup`, `row`, `rowgroup` |
| `table.tbody[].summary_placement` | `bottom`, `top` |
| `config.page_break_mode` | `avoid`, `allow`, `force-between-groups` (`force_between_groups`) |
| `config.dir` | `ltr`, `rtl`, `auto` |
| `border.*.style` | `none`, `hidden`, `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `double` |
| `font_weight` | `normal`, `bold`, `bolder`, `lighter`, or a number 1–1000 (JSON string or number) |
| `font_style` | `normal`, `italic`, `oblique` |
| `text_transform` | `none`, `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize` |
| `text_decoration` | `none`, `underline`, `overline`, `line-through` (`line_through`) |
| `white_space` | `normal`, `nowrap`, `pre`, `pre-wrap`, `pre-line`, `break-spaces` |
| `word_break` | `normal`, `break-all`, `keep-all`, `break-word` |
| `overflow`, `config.container_overflow` | `visible`, `hidden`, `clip`, `scroll`, `auto` |
| `text_overflow` | `clip`, `ellipsis` |
| conditional `selector.row_parity` | `even`, `odd` |
| conditional `selector.scope` | `tbody` (`body`), `thead` (`head`), `table` (`all`) |
| `typed_value.type` | `string` (`str`, `text`, `character`), `number` (`float`, `double`, `numeric`), `integer` (`int`), `boolean` (`bool`, `logical`), `date`, `datetime` (`timestamp`), `time`, `duration` |

## Colors

`color`, `background_color` and `border.*.color` (in style definitions, composition
overrides and conditional styles), and `config.rules.*.color`, accept, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace:

| Form | Examples |
|------|----------|
| CSS named color (all 148) | `red`, `steelblue`, `RebeccaPurple`, `grey` |
| `transparent` | paints nothing |
| Hex | `#abc`, `#abcd`, `#aabbcc`, `#aabbccdd` |
| `rgb()` / `rgba()`, comma syntax | `rgb(255, 0, 0)`, `rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5)`, `rgb(100%, 50%, 0%)` |
| `rgb()` / `rgba()`, space syntax | `rgb(255 0 0)`, `rgb(255 0 0 / 50%)` |
| `hsl()` / `hsla()` | `hsl(120, 100%, 25%)`, `hsl(120deg 100% 25% / 0.5)`; hue units `deg`, `grad`, `rad`, `turn` |

Out-of-range channels clamp, as in CSS. Writers receive the parsed color, never the
source text: HTML and SVG emit `#RRGGBB` (or `rgba()` when translucent), Typst keeps
alpha as `#RRGGBBAA`, and formats without alpha (LaTeX, RTF, DOCX, PPTX, ANSI) drop
it. A fully transparent color paints nothing in every format.

## Lengths

A length is a finite number followed by a unit, `px`, `pt`, `em`, `rem`, `in`, `cm`,
`mm`, `%` or `fr` (case-insensitive, no space before the unit), or `auto`. A bare
`0` is allowed; any other number needs a unit. Each field accepts only the forms
that make sense for it:

| Field | Units | `%` | `fr` | `auto` | Negative |
|-------|:-----:|:---:|:----:|:------:|:--------:|
| `column_spec[].width` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |
| `column_spec[].min_width`, `max_width` | ✓ | ✓ | | | |
| `config.table_width`, `container_width`, `container_height` | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ | |
| `image.width`, `image.height` (image nodes, in any content) | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ | |
| style `min_width`, `max_width`, `padding.*` (definitions, composition overrides, conditional styles) | ✓ | ✓ | | | |
| style `indent` | ✓ | ✓ | | | ✓ |
| style `border.*.width`, `config.rules.*.width` | ✓ | | | | |
| style `font_size` | ✓ | ✓ | | | |

`font_size` also accepts the CSS size keywords `xx-small`, `x-small`, `small`,
`medium`, `large`, `x-large`, `xx-large`, `xxx-large`, `smaller` and `larger`.

## How Validation Works

The validator materializes a **2D occupancy grid** for each section:

1. Allocate a `rows × cols` grid
2. Walk every cell in document order
3. For each cell with `rowspan=R, colspan=C` at position `(r, c)`:
   - Claim all positions `(r..r+R, c..c+C)`
   - If already occupied → `SPAN_OVERLAP` error
   - If out of bounds → `SPAN_OVERFLOW_RIGHT` / `SPAN_OVERFLOW_BOTTOM` error
4. Report any position no cell covers as `SPAN_GAP`

## Error Output

Each error includes the rule name, location, and a human-readable message. A
message says where the problem is as the IR does, counting from 0: `thead row 0`,
`tbody group 1 row 2` (a group's data rows), `tbody group 1 summary row 0` (its
summary rows), `the cell at tbody group 0 (row=1, col=2)`, `the label of tbody group 1`,
or a field's path, such as `column_spec[1].width` or `footer.footnotes[0]`.

```text
[COL_COUNT] tbody group 0 row 0 has 4 cells but config.table_cols is 3
[SPAN_OVERFLOW_RIGHT] Cell at tbody group 0 (row=1, col=2) has colspan=2 but table only has 3 columns (would need col index up to 3)
[SPAN_PLACEHOLDER_HAS_CONTENT] Placeholder cell at tbody group 0 (row=0, col=2) has non-empty content
[STYLE_REFS_VALID] style_id "bold" of the cell at tbody group 0 (row=1, col=0) is not defined in styles.defs or styles.compositions
[DUPLICATE_ID] footer.footnotes[1] has the id "n" of footer.footnotes[0]: footnote ids must be unique
[INVALID_LENGTH] column_spec[1].width is "-5px", which is not valid here: it is negative (expected a non-negative length (px, pt, em, rem, in, cm, mm), or a percentage, or a fraction (fr), or auto)
[INVALID_LANG] config.lang is "fr_CA", which is not a language tag: subtags are separated by `-`, not `_` (fr-CA, not fr_CA)
[IR_VERSION] ir_version is "2.0", IR 2, and this gridwell reads only IR 1.x (a newer gridwell may read it)
```

When the table is of a newer minor version, the errors end with a note: an error may
be something that version added (a keyword value this gridwell doesn't know is
`UNKNOWN_VALUE`).

```text
(the table is IR 1.3, newer than the IR 1.0 this gridwell reads: an error may be something a newer IR version added)
```

## Warnings

A valid table can still use a feature an output format can't express: LaTeX can't
align one cell to the bottom of its row, and Typst has no double borders. The writer
then draws something close, and you can ask for a **warning** first. A warning
doesn't fail validation or stop rendering.

Each warning for a feature has the rule id `UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`, the format, the feature (named as
in the [feature matrix](../guide/feature-matrix.qmd), or for a format's own limits, as
below), where the table uses it (the first place, and how many others), and what the
writer draws instead:

```text
[UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE] typst can't express border-double (head row 1, column 1 and 2 other places): Typst strokes have no double line; a double border is drawn solid
```

| Format | Feature | Warned for |
|--------|---------|------------|
| `latex` | `font-family` | A font family, anywhere. A cell or group label in a monospace family is `\texttt`, and `system-ui` and the like are drawn in no format: neither is warned |
| `latex` | `vertical-align` | A `middle` or `bottom` cell beside one that may be taller: it breaks lines, has raw LaTeX, sits in a column with a width, or is in a larger font size. A cell spanning rows is centered on them, so only `bottom` is warned there |
| `latex` | `border-styles` | A dashed or dotted left or right border on a cell or group label |
| `latex` | `lang` | A `config.lang`: the language is the document's, set up by babel or polyglossia |
| `latex` | `rtl` | A right-to-left table (`dir: rtl`, or `auto` with right-to-left text): it is written left to right |
| `typst` | `border-double` | A double border on a cell or group label |
| `typst`, `svg` | `image` | An image that isn't a PNG, JPEG, GIF or SVG `data:` URI (one linked by URL or path) |
| `rtf` | `image` | An image that isn't a PNG or JPEG `data:` URI |
| `docx` | `image` | An image that isn't a PNG, JPEG or GIF `data:` URI |
| `xlsx` | `image` | An image that isn't a PNG, JPEG or GIF `data:` URI alone in its cell or line, or one in a footnote |
| `latex`, `pptx`, `ansi` | `image` | Any image |
| `rtf` | `lang` | A `config.lang`: RTF's `\lang` takes a Windows language id, which the writer doesn't map tags to yet |
| `ansi` | `rtl` | A right-to-left table: a terminal shows the columns left to right |
| `xlsx` | `lang` | A `config.lang`: a spreadsheet's cells have no language |
| `xlsx` | `text-length` | Text over a cell's 32,767 characters (a footnote's counting its mark and the space after it): the rest is cut |
| `xlsx` | `rich-text-length` | Rich text within 32,767 characters that its formatting markup takes over them: it is written without its formatting |

A language or a direction is the table's as a whole, warned for at `the table`.
Places count from 1: `the title`, `the subtitle`, `header line 1`,
`head row 1, column 2`, `group 1 row 3, column 2`, `group 1 summary row 1, column 1`,
`the label of group 2`, `footnote 1`, `source note 1`. A row counts within its part of
the IR (the head, or a group's rows or summary rows), and a column within
`column_spec`, hidden columns included. A cell in a hidden column isn't drawn, so it
isn't warned for.

### A newer minor version

A table of a newer minor IR version than this gridwell reads renders, leaving out what
that version added. It is warned for first, for any format, with the rule id
`NEWER_IR_VERSION`:

```text
[NEWER_IR_VERSION] the table is IR 1.3, newer than the IR 1.0 this gridwell reads: anything a newer IR version added is left out (a newer gridwell may render it)
```

Python and R also warn when they parse such a table (a `UserWarning`, an R
`warning()`).

Warnings are for a valid table: asking for them for an invalid one is the same error
rendering it would be.

## Usage

::: {.panel-tabset}

### CLI

```bash
gridwell validate table.json
# Exit code 0 = valid, 1 = errors found
# Warnings for every format, or one (they don't change the exit code)
gridwell validate --to latex table.json
# convert prints its format's warnings to stderr
```

### Rust

```rust
let errors = table.validate();
// errors: Vec<ValidationError>
let warnings = gridwell_render::warnings(&table, Some("latex"))?;
// warnings: Vec<Warning>; None for every format
```

### Python

```python
errors = table.validate()
# errors: list[str]
warnings = table.warnings("latex")
# warnings: list[str]; table.warnings() for every format
```

### R

```r
errors <- gw_validate(tbl)
# errors: character vector
warnings <- gw_warnings(tbl, "latex")
# warnings: character vector; gw_warnings(tbl) for every format
```

### C

```c
GridwellError *invalid = gridwell_validate(table);
// null if valid, else an error listing every problem
GridwellError *err = NULL;
GridwellTextResult w = gridwell_warnings(table, "latex", &err);
// one warning per line ("" if none); NULL for every format
gridwell_free_text_result(w);
```

:::
